findings.reason: the plan's §1 representation is exactly these invariants (offsets monotone, one closure/kind per unit), and a single `PackedWall` type constructed by `pack_wall_units` would enforce them instead of leaving each consumer to re-derive them.
findings.text: `pack_wall_units` returns a bare `(vertices, offsets)` tuple and the "packed wall" survives only as parallel arrays `wall_unit_offsets`, `wall_unit_closed` and `_wall_unit_vessel` threaded through roughly 180 occurrences across `forward_operator.py`, `connectivity_boundary.py`, `topology.py`, `mast_chain_factory.py` and `frame/firstwall.py`

findings.reason: this wrapper is precisely the second implementation through which the picture/solve disagreement §5 claims to prevent returns, so the section must share the owner's containment or justify the fork.
findings.text: `inside_wall_units` re-implements the vessel-minus-material containment over `WallUnit`s rather than calling a shared function, and §5 gives no reason the containment could not be shared with the solver's path

findings.reason: the owner `nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py` should carry the pointwise occupiable-region test beside its `inside_polygon` and `build_wall_mask`, and the four seams should call it, so a point on an open material blade is judged by one rule rather than four.
findings.text: four divergent occupiable-region tests exist instead of one owned mechanism: `nova/equilibrium/connectivity_boundary.py:233` (`_points_inside_wall_units`, JAX, used by the solver and by `topology.py`), `nova/equilibrium/contour_tree_mesh.py:89` (`_inside_wall_units`, shapely `covers` union, open units ignored), `nova/equilibrium/steering_frames.py:540` (`_inside_occupiable_region`, closed units only), and `nova/media/sources/frame.py:56` (open-material line excluded)

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the "packed wall" is not a module; it is three parallel arrays threaded through the operator and its consumers with no type owning their invariants.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — four divergent implementations of occupiable-region containment exist across the seams, none in the declared reuse authority `nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py`, so the plan re-implements rather than extends the owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the sections under active design (§3 solver consumers) add receipt fields (`wall_unit_index`, `strike_unit`) but no CLI option, MCP view, public definition or refusal family, so no section adds counted surface and none must name a retirement.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase (the cited scout `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/nova/s19-labeller/wall-units-scout.md` exists) and reuses `WallUnit`/`build_wall_mask` from `nova/equilibrium/wall_mask.py`; no second wall type is authored and §6 makes citing that type a node contract.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — `nova/media/sources/frame.py:inside_wall_units` re-implements occupiable containment as a thin layer over `inside_polygon` instead of extending the shared mechanism, and §5 states no reason the solver's containment could not be shared.
